inputs.text:
Folks, we all know how the mainstream media likes to spin things, but let's look at the reality on the ground. We are told there was a ceasefire announced in Gaza five months ago, yet the conflict grinds on and the humanitarian situation remains dire, with civilians still caught in the crossfire. As 56-year-old Ahmed Baroud, a father of five currently displaced in Deir al-Balah, rightly points out about the daily reality there: “Drones never stop buzzing overhead, gunfire and shelling continue almost daily and naval boats fire towards fishermen.” 

This is the tragic cost of protracted conflict and the failure to establish true, lasting security and order. When leadership and basic civic structures break down, it is the family unit and ordinary people who bear the ultimate burden, stripped entirely from their prewar existence as life becomes dark and brutal. We must always prioritize strong borders, national security, and decisive action that restores stability rather than endless, unresolved cycles of violence that devastate communities and leave families shattered.
